newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: REPSOL HOPES TO EXTEND VENEZUELA OIL CONTRACT.
newsitem.headline: REPSOL HOPES TO EXTEND VENEZUELA OIL CONTRACT.

text.p: Spain's Repsol is hoping to extend the life of its contract to exploit Venezuela's Mene Grande oilfield if the the contract goes well, a company official said on Tuesday.

Repsol paid $330 million for the 20-year deal to produce crude oil on behalf of Venezuelan state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) and is currently putting together its field reactivation plan. It is also planning extensive exploration in the area surrounding the Mene Grande field, said Salvador Castella, Repsol's manager in Venezuela.
"I imagine if there are good relations there could be an opportunity to extend the contract, if both parties agree," he said in an interview with Reuters.
Discovered in 1914 on the south eastern shores of Lake Maracaibo in western Venezuela, Mene Grande currently produces 4,000 bpd from 154 active wells.
Castella said it was still too early to say what the potential production from the field was, citing a range from 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 60,000 bpd.
"This project has a low to medium risk. There is no production risk and it is in a very prolific zone," he said.
Repsol's cash bid for the contract was nearly double that of its nearest rival and provoked some surprise among other delegates during the bidding round in June.

But Castella said Repsol planned to add all 100 million barrels of the field's proven reserves to Repsol's books at the end of this year, equivalent to 12.5 percent of its end-1996 worldwide reserves.
Also, Repsol was hoping to significantly increase the figure since the field is located near some of Venezuela's most prolific oil areas.
If the company makes a discovery within the five-year exploration phase of the contract, it will have the right to exploit this new field for 20 years from the discovery date.
"Apart from the figures we are working out, there are other figures which we can't give until we have drilled, but we have great confidence in the exploration potential of the area," Castella said.
The minimum investment required in Mene grande is $20 million within three years, but Repsol expects to invest much more than that.
Castella said Repsol had no intention of buying the oil produced in Mene Grande and saw the contract as a straight exploration and production deal.
